report: The kidney tissue section shows hypercellular glomeruli, possibly due to inflammation or proliferation. Surrounding tubular structures exhibit atrophy or dilation, accompanied by interstitial expansion suggestive of fibrosis or edema. Scattered inflammatory cells indicate interstitial nephritis. Proteinaceous deposits hint at minimal change disease or focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. Diagnosis requires clinical correlation and additional testing.

evidence.title: Various antibody clones of Napsin A, TTF-1, and p40 in non-small cell lung carcinoma
evidence.text: This tissue-microarray study evaluated CK5, p63, and p40 as squamous markers and Napsin A and TTF-1 as lung adenocarcinoma markers. Reported performance varied by marker and antibody clone, and combining Napsin A with TTF-1 improved sensitivity.

evidence.title: Immunostaining for TTF-1, Napsin A, p40, and cytokeratin 5 aids differential diagnosis of NSCLC
evidence.text: The study compared marker combinations for separating lung adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma. TTF-1 and Napsin A supported adenocarcinoma, while p40 and CK5 supported squamous differentiation; the combined panel was more informative than a single stain.

evidence.title: Educational case: basal cell carcinoma and its histologic differential
evidence.text: Basal cell carcinoma shows dermal islands of basophilic tumor cells with peripheral nuclear palisading, stromal retraction, and loose mucinous stroma. Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma shows invasive islands of pleomorphic keratinocytes arising from the epidermis with prominent nucleoli and increased mitoses. Melanoma can show irregular nests and single pleomorphic pigmented melanocytes within the epidermis and dermis.

evidence.title: Colorectal carcinoma: pathologic aspects
evidence.text: Colorectal adenocarcinoma commonly forms malignant glands. Invasion can be accompanied by desmoplastic stroma, and glandular lumina frequently contain characteristic dirty necrosis. Benign colonic mucosa retains orderly crypt architecture and mature goblet cells without dysplasia.

evidence.title: Histologic features of Candida esophagitis
evidence.text: Candida esophagitis shows fungal hyphae, pseudohyphae, and spores along or invading squamous epithelium, often with neutrophilic inflammation, erosion, ulceration, and necrotic debris. PAS or Grocott methenamine silver stains help demonstrate fungal forms and distinguish Candida from viral esophagitis.

review.assessment: The vision-model outputs are entirely inconsistent with the provided pathology report, which describes benign/inflammatory kidney disease rather than malignancy.
rationale: The de-identified report describes hypercellular glomeruli, interstitial nephritis, and potential minimal change disease or FSGS, which are non-malignant renal pathologies.
None of the candidate labels (various carcinomas) are supported by the report's description of inflammation, fibrosis, and proteinaceous deposits.
The retrieved literature [PMC:3418538-ColorectalMorphology, PMID:26447895] describes malignant features (dirty necrosis, TTF-1/p40 markers) that are absent from the case report.
discrepancies: All vision models (CONCH, MUSK, PLIP, QUILTNET) predicted various carcinomas, whereas the report describes a non-neoplastic kidney condition.
The candidate labels provided do not include the benign renal pathologies suggested by the report.
recommended_review: Human pathologist review to reconcile the discrepancy between the report (benign/inflammatory kidney disease) and the model predictions (malignancy).
Clinical correlation and additional testing as suggested in the report.
limitations: The candidate label set is restricted to malignancies, making it impossible to select a label that matches the benign findings in the report.
